Ricardo grew up in a full, loud household where his mother's love came free but his father's warmth had to be earned — unload the truck, work the pit, and there were stories and a hand on the back of his neck at dinner; spend the Saturday hunched over alebrijes at the kitchen table and the room went quiet around him. His father carried the family the only way he knew how, with his back and his hours, so a son who drew all day looked to him like a son who would need carrying. When Ricardo dropped out at seventeen, the two of them barely spoke for the better part of a year, and even after they made peace he never showed his father a sketchbook again.

Precipitating.
